# Adjudication Task — Chapter 530

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃530화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|하남은 그야말로 중원(中原)이라 불릴 만한 곳이다.
  6|
  7|황하를 따라 문명이 시작된 이래 수천 년간 천하의 중심지였고, 오랜 시간 동안 들불처럼 일어나고 스러져 간 아홉 개 왕조의 도읍이기도 하니까.
  8|
  9|그렇다 보니 무림맹이 공식적으로 재건되고, 흉흉한 전운(戰運)이 감돌기 시작한 지금에도 하남성은 활기를 잃지 않았다.
 10|
 11|아니, 오히려 그와 정반대의 흐름으로 흘러가고 있었다.
 12|
 13|“기분 탓인가, 사람들도 더 많아지고 분위기도 괜찮은데요?”
 14|
 15|혁무진의 말은 사실이었다. 넓은 대로변은 사람들로 가득했고 표정에는 딱히 큰 근심을 찾기 힘들었다.
 16|
 17|간혹 병장기를 패용한 채 거리를 오가는 무림인들을 불안한 시선으로 힐끗거리는 사람들이 있었지만 그뿐이다.
 18|
 19|나는 죽립을 더 깊게 눌러쓰며 중얼거렸다.
 20|
 21|“그러네.”
 22|
 23|“희한하네요. 얼마 전까지는 그래도 분위기가 영 아니었는데. 이게 폭풍전야인지 뭔지 하는 그겁니까?”
 24|
 25|“……미친놈아. 아예 무슨 일 터지라고 불공을 드려라.”
 26|
 27|“상황을 고려해 보면 딱히 틀린 말도 아니지 않습니까.”
 28|
 29|그건 맞다. 하지만 혁무진이 간과하고 있는 사실 또한 있었다. 이놈의 뒤통수를 한 대 칠까 말까 고민하던 나는 고개를 가로저었다.
 30|
 31|“그보다는 이제 저 사람들도 알게 됐다고 봐야지.”
 32|
 33|“뭘요?”
 34|
 35|“이곳, 하남이야말로 천하에서 가장 안전한 곳이라는 사실.”
 36|
 37|“……아.”
 38|
 39|양민들의 시선으로 보는 무림인이란 족속들은 통제되지 않는 맹수와 같다.
 40|
 41|하지만 지금 하남에 있는 무림인 중 대부분은 의협과 대의, 그리고 무림맹이라는 이름으로 하나가 되어 뭉친 자들이다.
 42|
 43|심지어 그런 이들의 숫자가 수십 수백도 아니고 무려 수천이었다.
 44|
 45|양민 입장에서는 무림인들끼리 전쟁이 일어났다는 소식에 불안했겠지만, 이제는 빠르게 안정되어 가는 추세였다.
 46|
 47|‘현대였다면 이 정도로 분위기가 좋진 않았겠지.’
 48|
 49|미국과 러시아 사이에 전쟁이 일어났다고 생각해 봐라.
 50|
 51|전쟁 개시와 동시에 모스크바나 워싱턴 DC의 시민들은 죽어라 도망치거나 하늘만 올려다보고 있을 거다. 대륙 간 탄도 미사일이나 핵이 언제쯤 날아올까 가늠하면서.
 52|
 53|‘그렇다고 하남이 완전히 안전하리란 보장도 없지만.’
 54|
 55|암천이 천하의 절반을 쓸어 버리며 하남까지 도착한다?
 56|
 57|아주 가능성이 없지는 않다. 무림맹이 결성되고 수많은 무림인이 한 깃발 아래 섰다 한들 전쟁의 결과까지 알 수는 없는 법이니까.
 58|
 59|하지만 그것보다 더 큰 문제는 그 외의 방법이 존재한다는 것이다.
 60|
 61|‘이동진. 아니, 워프 마법진이라고 불러야 하나.’
 62|
 63|아직 모두에게 알려지지는 않은, 믿기 힘들면서도 불편한 진실.
 64|
 65|이와 같은 진실은 경각심을 일깨워 주기도 하지만, 때때로 엄청난 혼돈과 충격을 동반한다. 그래서 아직 공표되지 않는 거겠지만.
 66|
 67|‘그때가 되면 지금처럼 웃고만 있지는 않겠지.’
 68|
 69|쓰게 입맛을 다신 나는 문득 주위를 둘러보았다.
 70|
 71|신기한 눈빛으로 지나가는 무림인들을 바라보는 아이와 때아닌 호황에 힘입어 신이 난 장사치. 그리고 긴장과 흥분이 뒤섞인 얼굴로 대로변을 오가는 무림인들.
 72|
 73|적어도 이들 중 암천에 관한 모든 정보를 아는 사람은 없다.
 74|
 75|깊은 비밀을 아는 자들은 이미 자신들의 새로운 맹주와 함께 언제 끝날지 모를 회의를 이어 가고 있으니까.
 76|
 77|“조장님?”
 78|
 79|“무슨 생각을 그렇게 하고 있어? 괜히 사람들 쳐다보게.”
 80|
 81|“……별거 아냐. 가자.”
 82|
 83|잠깐 넋을 놓고 있었던 모양이다. 짧은 상념에서 깨어난 나는 재차 걸음을 옮겼다.
 84|
 85|사람들이 우글거리는 대로변 중앙에서 혼자 멀거니 서 있으면 이목을 끌기 마련이다.
 86|
 87|아니나 다를까, 벌써 눈썰미가 예리한 몇몇 인물들은 이쪽을 쳐다보는 중이었다.
 88|
 89|‘평범한 무림인은 아니다. 고수야.’
 90|
 91|그렇다고 암천의 끄나풀이라 생각하는 건 과대 해석이다.
 92|
 93|당당하게 무복을 차려입고 병장기를 패용한 그들에게서는 하나같이 정순한 기운들이 느껴졌다.
 94|
 95|“저기, 조장님.”
 96|
 97|등 뒤에서 들려온 혁무진의 낮은 목소리가 귓가를 파고든다. 하지만 나는 아무런 일도 없다는 듯 계속해서 걸음을 옮겼다.
 98|
 99|“괜찮아. 그냥 가.”
100|
101|“알고 계셨어요?”
102|
103|“당연히.”
104|
105|“그래도 저는 좀 불안한데요.”
106|
107|혁무진의 걱정도 이해가 됐다.
108|
109|숭산결의 이후 나도 제법 유명인사가 된 상태다.
110|
111|이미 전부터 산서잠룡, 열화신룡이라는 별호를 천하 무림에 각인시켰지만, 수천여 명의 군웅들 앞에서 무림맹의 깃발을 들어 올림으로써 확실한 눈도장을 찍었다.
112|
113|구파일방과 오대세가의 주인들만큼은 아니어도, 명문대파의 어지간한 장로급 고수보다 이름과 얼굴이 팔린 것이다.
114|
115|“불안하긴 무슨. 그냥 못 본 척하고 지나가.”
116|
117|“아니, 진짜 큰일 날 것 같아서 그래요.”
118|
119|계속되는 혁무진의 걱정에 궁기방이 혀를 찼다.
120|
121|“간댕이가 그렇게 작아서야. 얼굴 좀 알아본다고 무슨 큰일이 나냐? 그냥 좀 귀찮아질 뿐이지. 이럴까 봐 죽립까지 쓴 거 아냐.”
122|
123|가볍게 핀잔을 준 궁기방이 나를 바라보며 물었다.
124|
125|“저놈 저거 왜 저래?”
126|
127|“놔둬. 그래도 기특하잖아. 미리 눈치채고 걱정한다는 게.”
128|
129|“……뭐. 그건 그렇지만.”
130|
131|나는 내심 흐뭇하게 웃었다.
132|
133|평소에 표현을 잘 안 해서 그렇지, 혁무진은 나한테 있어서 아픈 손가락이다.
134|
135|무림에 온 이후로 가장 오랜 시간을 함께하며 온갖 고생을 한 터라 마음이 쓰일 수밖에 없었…….
136|
137|“환장하겠네. 지금 무슨 소리세요?”
138|
139|“응?”
140|
141|“뭐?”
142|
143|반문하는 나와 궁기방을 향해, 혁무진이 창백해진 안색으로 말을 이었다.
144|
145|“아까부터 똥 마려워 죽겠는데 이상한 말씀들만 하시고. 어후, 진짜.”
146|
147|“……!”
148|
149|“……!”
150|
151|기특하긴 시벌.
152|
153|큰일 날 것 같다고 한 게 진짜 큰일 말하는 거였네.
154|
155|순간 할 말을 잃어버린 나와 궁기방의 모습에, 혁무진이 식은땀을 흘리며 앞장서서 걸음을 옮겼다.
156|
157|“모인다는 장소가 어딥니까. 어서 빨리! 이러다가 나와요!”
158|
159|미친 기백 보소. 전투 때도 못 봤던 처절한 모습에 궁기방이 반사적으로 손가락을 들어 한 건물을 가리켰다.
160|
161|“저, 저기긴 한데.”
162|
163|“저거? 삼 층 객잔?”
164|
165|“어? 어어.”
166|
167|“으흣. 그럼 저 먼저 갑니다. 응가아아앗!”
168|
169|마지막의 외침은 똥을 참고자 하는 의지인가. 마지막 괄약근을 태워 터트리는 부스터인가.
170|
171|신형을 비틀거리면서도 엄청난 속도로 인파를 헤집는 녀석의 모습에 궁기방이 중얼거렸다.
172|
173|“취팔선보(醉八旋步)……?”
174|
175|“……제발 개소리하지 마. 그냥 똥 마려운 거니까.”
176|
177|하느님. 부처님. 왜 제 곁에는 병신들밖에 없나요.
178|
179|마음 깊이 한탄한 나는 혁무진이 향하고 있는 삼 층 객잔을 바라보았다.
180|
181|멀지 않은 거리. 이곳까지 오며 진정되었던 가슴 한구석이 울렁거리는 기분이다.
182|
183|“……한 달? 아니, 두 달 만인가.”
184|
185|나도 모르게 흘러나온 중얼거림에 궁기방의 눈이 게슴츠레해졌다.
186|
187|“오호.”
188|
189|“뭐, 새꺄.”
190|
191|“설마 내가 생각하는 그것인가?”
192|
193|“너 생각도 할 수 있는 동물이었냐?”
194|
195|“맞지?”
196|
197|“맞을래?”
198|
199|“하긴. 그때 분위기가 좀 묘하긴 했지.”
200|
201|“묘지 정해 줘?”
202|
203|“교묘하게 피해 가는 것을 보니 맞는 것 같군.”
204|
205|“교묘하게 피해도 피할 수 없을 만큼 빠르게 맞고 싶니?”
206|
207|“푸흐흐. 이 광경을 혁가 놈을 봤어야 했는데.”
208|
209|“……아니. 그러니까 이게. 후. 됐다.”
210|
211|이쯤 되면 맞기 싫어서라도 슬쩍 말을 돌렸을 놈이 오늘은 다르다.
212|
213|바람 빠지는 듯한 웃음소리와 함께 힐끗거리는 궁기방의 모습에 주먹이 불끈 쥐어졌지만, 이상하게도 때릴 마음이 들지 않았다.
214|
215|“푸흐흐흐흐.”
216|
217|“…….”
218|
219|빡!
220|
221|웃는 꼴을 보고 있자니 때릴 마음이 아주 펑펑 솟구치네.
222|
223|나는 비명도 못 지르고 명치를 부여잡은 궁기방의 뒷덜미를 붙잡고 들어 올렸다.
224|
225|“그래서. 저기 맞지? 삼 층 객잔.”
226|
227|“어흑. 마, 맞다.”
228|
229|“난 음식 먹으러 가는 거다. 배고파서 가는 거야.”
230|
231|“아, 안다.”
232|
233|“곤륜운룡인지 뭔지 하는 걔도 왔다며. 오랜만에 걔 보러 가는 거야. 겸사겸사 황보 뭐시기랑 교분도 쌓고.”
234|
235|“……명심하겠다.”
236|
237|“처신 잘하라고. 십봉룡이 구봉룡 되기 싫으면.”
238|
239|이만하면 정신교육은 똑바로 된 것 같다. 풀려난 궁기방이 얻어맞은 부위를 쓰다듬으며 중얼거렸다.
240|
241|“악독한 놈.”
242|
243|“뭐라고?”
244|
245|“아, 아무것도 아니다.”
246|
247|씨알도 안 먹힐 대답을 한 궁기방이 황급히 화제를 돌렸다.
248|
249|“그나저나 기대되는군. 네가 온 것을 알면 모두 쌍수를 들고 환영할 거다.”
250|
251|“별로 상관없어. 쌍수를 들고 환영하든, 말든.”
252|
253|곤륜운룡도, 황보세가의 소가주라던 그놈도 딱히 신경 쓰지 않는다.
254|
255|다만…… 한 사람만큼은 진심으로 반겨 줬으면 하는 바람이다.
256|
257|하지만 내 대답을 잘못 이해한 궁기방은 다급하게 말을 이었다.
258|
259|“아니다! 황보악 그자가 좀 밥맛이긴 한데, 그래도 네가 여기까지 왔다는 소식을 들으면 맨발로 뛰쳐나와서…….”
260|
261|하지만 궁기방의 말은 끝까지 이어지지 못했다.
262|
263|콰앙!
264|
265|순간 터져 나온 굉음이 궁기방의 목소리와 시끌벅적하던 대로변의 소음을 모조리 집어삼켰다.
266|
267|찰나라고 부를 수도 없을 만큼 짧은 시간 속, 잠깐 내려앉았던 침묵이 깨어지는 것은 순식간이었다.
268|
269|“으아악!”
270|
271|“꺄아아아아!”
272|
273|“고월루(古月樓)! 고월루가……!”
274|
275|비명이 난무하고 수많은 사람이 메뚜기 떼처럼 사방으로 흩어진다.
276|
277|하지만 나는 그 자리에 우뚝 서서 응시하고 있었다.
278|
279|‘고월루.’
280|
281|내게는 똑똑히 보인다. 오늘의 만남이 예정되어있는 바로 삼 층 객잔의 일부가 뻥 뚫려 있는 모습이.
282|
283|소나기처럼 쏟아지는 자재와 먼지구름 사이를 뚫고 튕겨져 나오는 누군가의 신형이.
284|
285|쐐애애애액! 콰광!
286|
287|얼마 떨어지지 않은 거리. 길거리에 놓여 있던 좌판이 박살나고 땅이 깊게 파였다.
288|
289|그리고 가까스로 신형을 바로잡으며 자리에서 일어나는 한 사내가 있었다.
290|
291|투두두둑.
292|
293|‘누구지?’
294|
295|갈기갈기 찢어진 무복과 벗겨져 나간 가죽신. 잘생긴 얼굴에는 분노와 낭패가 가득하다.
296|
297|“감히, 감히 이 찢어 죽일 놈이……!”
298|
299|바로 그때였다.
300|
301|악문 잇새로 끓어오르는 음성을 내뱉은 사내의 모습에, 궁기방이 입을 딱 벌리며 외쳤다.

“Pfft, pfft, pfft.”

[P99]
“…”

[P100]
*Bam!*

[P101]
Watching him laugh brought the urge right back.

[P102]
He couldn’t even scream. I grabbed him by the back of the neck and hauled him up as he clutched his solar plexus.

[P103]
“So. That’s the place, right? The three-story inn.”

[P104]
“Urgh. Y-yes.”

[P105]
“I’m going for the food. Because I’m hungry.”

[P106]
“I-I know.”

[P107]
“That Kunlun Cloud Dragon guy is there too, right? I haven’t seen him in a while. And while I’m at it, I can get to know that Hwangbo fellow.”

[P108]
“…I’ll remember that.”

[P109]
“See that you do. Unless you want the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes to become the Nine Dragons and Phoenixes.”

[P110]
That seemed to drive the lesson home. Once I let him go, Gung Gibang rubbed the spot I’d hit.

[P111]
“Vicious bastard.”

[P112]
“What was that?”

[P113]
“N-nothing.”

[P114]
As if that would fool me. Gung Gibang hastily changed the subject.

[P115]
“Anyway, I’m looking forward to it. When they hear you’ve come, they’ll welcome you with open arms.”

[P116]
“I don’t care whether they do or not.”

[P117]
I wasn’t particularly interested in the Kunlun Cloud Dragon or that Lesser Family Head of the Hwangbo Family.

[P118]
There was, though, one person I hoped would be genuinely glad to see me.

[P119]
Gung Gibang took my answer the wrong way.

[P120]
“No! Hwangbo Ak is a bit of a pain, but once he hears you came all this way, he’ll come running out barefoot and—”

[P121]
He never finished.

[P122]
*Boom!*

[P123]
A thunderous crash swallowed his voice and every sound on the bustling street.

[P124]
A silence too brief to call an instant fell, then broke.

[P125]
“Aaah!”

[P126]
“Eeeeeek!”

[P127]
“Gowolru! Gowolru is…!”

[P128]
People screamed and scattered in every direction like a swarm of locusts.

[P129]
I stood where I was and stared.

[P130]
*Gowolru.*

[P131]
I could see it clearly. A section of the three-story inn where we were supposed to meet had been blown wide open.

[P132]
Someone came hurtling out through a shower of debris and a cloud of dust.

[P133]
*Whoosh! Crash!*

[P134]
A street stall not far away shattered, and a deep gouge opened in the ground.

[P135]
A man managed to right himself and get to his feet.

[P136]
*Rattle, rattle.*

[P137]
*Who’s that?*

[P138]
His martial uniform was torn to shreds, and his leather shoes had come off. His handsome face was filled with fury and dismay.

[P139]
“How dare you… I’ll tear you apart…!”

[P140]
Gung Gibang gaped at the man, who was speaking through clenched teeth.

[P141]
“H-Hwangbo Ak!”

[P142]
“…?”

[P143]
“What are you doing out here?”

[P144]
*What? That’s Hwangbo Ak?*

[P145]
Hwangbo Ak faltered at the sound of his name. I looked him up and down.

[P146]
“He did come running out barefoot.”

[P147]
Was this a surprise for me? Some impromptu welcome from the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes?

[P148]
Judging by the way Hwangbo Ak’s face twisted, probably not.

[P149]
“What did you just say?”

[P150]
“Oh. Sorry. I didn’t mean it that way.”

[P151]
“You damned bastard…”

[P152]
“You look busy. Let’s talk later. Ah, here it comes.”

[P153]
“What?”

[P154]
His confusion lasted only an instant. He seemed to remember something, and urgency and horror crossed his face.

[P155]
*Whoooosh—boom!*

[P156]
Something enormous shot through the air and slammed into Hwangbo Ak.

[P157]
I could tell how fast it was moving, and how much force it carried, just from the sound. He would have been hard-pressed to deal with it while fully alert. Distracted as he was, the result was inevitable.

[P158]
“Guhk!”

[P159]
Hwangbo Ak went flying, spraying blood. A massive shadow moved to pursue him.

[P160]
What should I do? I didn’t have to think long.

[P161]
*Never a quiet day around here.*

[P162]
I stepped forward with a soft sigh.

[P163]
An enormous man blocked out the sun, casting a vast shadow over me. He looked down at me with eyes as big as bowls.

[P164]
“You. Move.”

[P165]
I answered calmly.

[P166]
“Me. Don’t want to.”

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

That didn’t make them Dark Heaven’s agents. They wore martial uniforms and carried their weapons openly, and I could sense pure qi from every one of them.

[P42]
“Captain.”

[P43]
Hyuk Mujin’s voice came quietly from behind me. I kept walking as though nothing was wrong.

[P44]
“It’s fine. Just keep going.”

[P45]
“You knew?”

[P46]
“Of course.”

[P47]
“I’m still worried.”

[P48]
I understood why. Since the Mount Song Resolution, I’d become something of a celebrity.

[P49]
The names Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi and Blazing Flame Divine Dragon had already spread throughout Murim. Raising the Alliance flag before thousands of martial heroes had made my face just as recognizable.

[P50]
I wasn’t on the level of the heads of the Nine Sects and One Gang or the Five Great Families, but more people knew my name and face than those of most Elder-level masters from major factions.

[P51]
“What’s there to worry about? Pretend you haven’t noticed them and keep walking.”

[P52]
“No, I’m worried something really bad is going to happen.”

[P53]
Gung Gibang clicked his tongue.

[P54]
“What a coward. What’s the worst that can happen if they recognize him? We’ll be inconvenienced, that’s all. Why do you think he’s wearing the bamboo hat?”

[P55]
He glanced at me. “What’s gotten into him?”

[P56]
“Leave him alone. It’s kind of touching that he noticed them first and started worrying.”

[P57]
“…I suppose.”

[P58]
I smiled to myself.

[P59]
Hyuk Mujin didn’t usually show it, but I had a soft spot for him. Since coming to Murim, I’d spent more time with him than anyone else, and we’d been through all kinds of trouble together. Of course I cared about—

[P60]
“This is driving me crazy. What are you two talking about?”

[P61]
“Huh?”

[P62]
“What?”

[P63]
Hyuk Mujin looked at Gung Gibang and me, his face pale.

[P64]
“I’ve been about to shit myself this whole time, and you two keep saying the weirdest things. Seriously.”

[P65]
“…!”

[P66]
“…!”

[P67]
Touching, my ass.

[P68]
When he said something bad was going to happen, he’d meant *that*.

[P69]
As Gung Gibang and I stared at him, speechless, Hyuk Mujin broke into a cold sweat and hurried ahead.

[P70]
“Where are we meeting? Hurry! It’s coming out!”

[P71]
Look at that determination. I’d never seen him look so desperate, even in a fight. Gung Gibang pointed at a building on reflex.

[P72]
“O-over there.”

[P73]
“That one? The three-story inn?”

[P74]
“Uh? Yeah.”

[P75]
“Then I’m going ahead. Pooooop!”

[P76]
Was that last cry sheer determination to hold it in? Or a booster powered by the last of his sphincter’s strength?

[P77]
Hyuk Mujin staggered as he wove through the crowd at incredible speed. Gung Gibang muttered, “Drunken Eight-Immortals Step…?”

[P78]
“…Please don’t talk bullshit. He just needs to shit.”

[P79]
God. Buddha. Why am I surrounded by idiots?

[P80]
Lamenting my fate, I looked toward the three-story inn Hyuk Mujin was heading for.

[P81]
It wasn’t far. A feeling that had settled during the journey stirred in my chest again.

[P82]
“…A month? No, has it been two?”

[P83]
Gung Gibang narrowed his eyes at my unguarded mutter.

[P84]
“Oh-ho.”

[P85]
“What, you bastard?”

[P86]
“Is it what I think it is?”

[P87]
“You can think?”

[P88]
“I’m right, aren’t I?”

[P89]
“Want to get hit?”

[P90]
“Come to think of it, things were a little strange between you two back then.”

[P91]
“Want me to pick out your grave?”

[P92]
“That clever dodge tells me I’m right.”

[P93]
“Want me to hit you so fast you can’t dodge, clever or not?”

[P94]
“Pfft. Hyuk should’ve seen this.”

[P95]
“…No, it’s not— Ah, forget it.”

[P96]
Normally, Gung Gibang would have changed the subject by now, if only to avoid getting hit. Today he kept snickering and glancing at me.

[P97]
My fist clenched, but strangely, I didn’t feel like using it.

[P98]
“Pfft, pfft, pfft.”

[P99]
“…”

[P100]
*Bam!*

[P101]
Watching him laugh brought the urge right back.

[P102]
He couldn’t even scream. I grabbed him by the back of the neck and hauled him up as he clutched his solar plexus.

[P103]
“So. That’s the place, right? The three-story inn.”

[P104]
“Urgh. Y-yes.”

[P105]
“I’m going for the food. Because I’m hungry.”

[P106]
“I-I know.”

[P107]
“That Kunlun Cloud Dragon guy is there too, right? I haven’t seen him in a while. And while I’m at it, I can get to know that Hwangbo fellow.”

[P108]
“…I’ll remember that.”

[P109]
“See that you do. Unless you want the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes to become the Nine Dragons and Phoenixes.”

[P110]
That seemed to drive the lesson home. Once I let him go, Gung Gibang rubbed the spot I’d hit.

[P111]
“Vicious bastard.”

[P112]
“What was that?”

[P113]
“N-nothing.”

[P114]
As if that would fool me. Gung Gibang hastily changed the subject.

[P115]
“Anyway, I’m looking forward to it. When they hear you’ve come, they’ll welcome you with open arms.”

[P116]
“I don’t care whether they do or not.”

[P117]
I wasn’t particularly interested in the Kunlun Cloud Dragon or that Lesser Family Head of the Hwangbo Family.

[P118]
There was, though, one person I hoped would be genuinely glad to see me.

[P119]
Gung Gibang took my answer the wrong way.

[P120]
“No! Hwangbo Ak is a bit of a pain, but once he hears you came all this way, he’ll come running out barefoot and—”

[P121]
He never finished.

[P122]
*Boom!*

[P123]
A thunderous crash swallowed his voice and every sound on the bustling street.

[P124]
A silence too brief to call an instant fell, then broke.

[P125]
“Aaah!”

[P126]
“Eeeeeek!”

[P127]
“Gowolru! Gowolru is…!”

[P128]
People screamed and scattered in every direction like a swarm of locusts.

[P129]
I stood where I was and stared.

[P130]
*Gowolru.*

[P131]
I could see it clearly. A section of the three-story inn where we were supposed to meet had been blown wide open.

[P132]
Someone came hurtling out through a shower of debris and a cloud of dust.

[P133]
*Whoosh! Crash!*

[P134]
A street stall not far away shattered, and a deep gouge opened in the ground.

[P135]
A man managed to right himself and get to his feet.

[P136]
*Rattle, rattle.*

[P137]
*Who’s that?*

[P138]
His martial uniform was torn to shreds, and his leather shoes had come off. His handsome face was filled with fury and dismay.

[P139]
“How dare you… I’ll tear you apart…!”

[P140]
Gung Gibang gaped at the man, who was speaking through clenched teeth.

[P141]
“H-Hwangbo Ak!”

[P142]
“…?”

[P143]
“What are you doing out here?”

[P144]
*What? That’s Hwangbo Ak?*

[P145]
Hwangbo Ak faltered at the sound of his name. I looked him up and down.

[P146]
“He did come running out barefoot.”

[P147]
Was this a surprise for me? Some impromptu welcome from the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes?

[P148]
Judging by the way Hwangbo Ak’s face twisted, probably not.

[P149]
“What did you just say?”

[P150]
“Oh. Sorry. I didn’t mean it that way.”

[P151]
“You damned bastard…”

[P152]
“You look busy. Let’s talk later. Ah, here it comes.”

[P153]
“What?”

[P154]
His confusion lasted only an instant. He seemed to remember something, and urgency and horror crossed his face.

[P155]
*Whoooosh—boom!*

[P156]
Something enormous shot through the air and slammed into Hwangbo Ak.

[P157]
I could tell how fast it was moving, and how much force it carried, just from the sound. He would have been hard-pressed to deal with it while fully alert. Distracted as he was, the result was inevitable.

[P158]
“Guhk!”

[P159]
Hwangbo Ak went flying, spraying blood. A massive shadow moved to pursue him.

[P160]
What should I do? I didn’t have to think long.

[P161]
*Never a quiet day around here.*

[P162]
I stepped forward with a soft sigh.

[P163]
An enormous man blocked out the sun, casting a vast shadow over me. He looked down at me with eyes as big as bowls.

[P164]
“You. Move.”

[P165]
I answered calmly.

[P166]
“Me. Don’t want to.”

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.

[P65]
“…!”

[P66]
“…!”

[P67]
Touching, my ass.

[P68]
When he said something bad was going to happen, he’d meant *that*.

[P69]
As Gung Gibang and I stared at him, speechless, Hyuk Mujin broke into a cold sweat and hurried ahead.

[P70]
“Where are we meeting? Hurry! It’s coming out!”

[P71]
Look at that determination. I’d never seen him look so desperate, even in a fight. Gung Gibang pointed at a building on reflex.

[P72]
“O-over there.”

[P73]
“That one? The three-story inn?”

[P74]
“Uh? Yeah.”

[P75]
“Then I’m going ahead. Pooooop!”

[P76]
Was that last cry sheer determination to hold it in? Or a booster powered by the last of his sphincter’s strength?

[P77]
Hyuk Mujin staggered as he wove through the crowd at incredible speed. Gung Gibang muttered, “Drunken Eight-Immortals Step…?”

[P78]
“…Please don’t talk bullshit. He just needs to shit.”

[P79]
God. Buddha. Why am I surrounded by idiots?

[P80]
Lamenting my fate, I looked toward the three-story inn Hyuk Mujin was heading for.

[P81]
It wasn’t far. A feeling that had settled during the journey stirred in my chest again.

[P82]
“…A month? No, has it been two?”

[P83]
Gung Gibang narrowed his eyes at my unguarded mutter.

[P84]
“Oh-ho.”

[P85]
“What, you bastard?”

[P86]
“Is it what I think it is?”

[P87]
“You can think?”

[P88]
“I’m right, aren’t I?”

[P89]
“Want to get hit?”

[P90]
“Come to think of it, things were a little strange between you two back then.”

[P91]
“Want me to pick out your grave?”

[P92]
“That clever dodge tells me I’m right.”

[P93]
“Want me to hit you so fast you can’t dodge, clever or not?”

[P94]
“Pfft. Hyuk should’ve seen this.”

[P95]
“…No, it’s not— Ah, forget it.”

[P96]
Normally, Gung Gibang would have changed the subject by now, if only to avoid getting hit. Today he kept snickering and glancing at me.

[P97]
My fist clenched, but strangely, I didn’t feel like using it.

[P98]
“Pfft, pfft, pfft.”

[P99]
“…”

[P100]
*Bam!*

[P101]
Watching him laugh brought the urge right back.

[P102]
He couldn’t even scream. I grabbed him by the back of the neck and hauled him up as he clutched his solar plexus.

[P103]
“So. That’s the place, right? The three-story inn.”

[P104]
“Urgh. Y-yes.”

[P105]
“I’m going for the food. Because I’m hungry.”

[P106]
“I-I know.”

[P107]
“That Kunlun Cloud Dragon guy is there too, right? I haven’t seen him in a while. And while I’m at it, I can get to know that Hwangbo fellow.”

[P108]
“…I’ll remember that.”

[P109]
“See that you do. Unless you want the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes to become the Nine Dragons and Phoenixes.”

[P110]
That seemed to drive the lesson home. Once I let him go, Gung Gibang rubbed the spot I’d hit.

[P111]
“Vicious bastard.”

[P112]
“What was that?”

[P113]
“N-nothing.”

[P114]
As if that would fool me. Gung Gibang hastily changed the subject.

[P115]
“Anyway, I’m looking forward to it. When they hear you’ve come, they’ll welcome you with open arms.”

[P116]
“I don’t care whether they do or not.”

[P117]
I wasn’t particularly interested in the Kunlun Cloud Dragon or that Lesser Family Head of the Hwangbo Family.

[P118]
There was, though, one person I hoped would be genuinely glad to see me.

[P119]
Gung Gibang took my answer the wrong way.

[P120]
“No! Hwangbo Ak is a bit of a pain, but once he hears you came all this way, he’ll come running out barefoot and—”

[P121]
He never finished.

[P122]
*Boom!*

[P123]
A thunderous crash swallowed his voice and every sound on the bustling street.

[P124]
A silence too brief to call an instant fell, then broke.

[P125]
“Aaah!”

[P126]
“Eeeeeek!”

[P127]
“Gowolru! Gowolru is…!”

[P128]
People screamed and scattered in every direction like a swarm of locusts.

[P129]
I stood where I was and stared.

[P130]
*Gowolru.*

[P131]
I could see it clearly. A section of the three-story inn where we were supposed to meet had been blown wide open.

[P132]
Someone came hurtling out through a shower of debris and a cloud of dust.

[P133]
*Whoosh! Crash!*

[P134]
A street stall not far away shattered, and a deep gouge opened in the ground.

[P135]
A man managed to right himself and get to his feet.

[P136]
*Rattle, rattle.*

[P137]
*Who’s that?*

[P138]
His martial uniform was torn to shreds, and his leather shoes had come off. His handsome face was filled with fury and dismay.

[P139]
“How dare you… I’ll tear you apart…!”

[P140]
Gung Gibang gaped at the man, who was speaking through clenched teeth.

[P141]
“H-Hwangbo Ak!”

[P142]
“…?”

[P143]
“What are you doing out here?”

[P144]
*What? That’s Hwangbo Ak?*

[P145]
Hwangbo Ak faltered at the sound of his name. I looked him up and down.

[P146]
“He did come running out barefoot.”

[P147]
Was this a surprise for me? Some impromptu welcome from the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes?

[P148]
Judging by the way Hwangbo Ak’s face twisted, probably not.

[P149]
“What did you just say?”

[P150]
“Oh. Sorry. I didn’t mean it that way.”

[P151]
“You damned bastard…”

[P152]
“You look busy. Let’s talk later. Ah, here it comes.”

[P153]
“What?”

[P154]
His confusion lasted only an instant. He seemed to remember something, and urgency and horror crossed his face.

[P155]
*Whoooosh—boom!*

[P156]
Something enormous shot through the air and slammed into Hwangbo Ak.

[P157]
I could tell how fast it was moving, and how much force it carried, just from the sound. He would have been hard-pressed to deal with it while fully alert. Distracted as he was, the result was inevitable.

[P158]
“Guhk!”

[P159]
Hwangbo Ak went flying, spraying blood. A massive shadow moved to pursue him.

[P160]
What should I do? I didn’t have to think long.

[P161]
*Never a quiet day around here.*

[P162]
I stepped forward with a soft sigh.

[P163]
An enormous man blocked out the sun, casting a vast shadow over me. He looked down at me with eyes as big as bowls.

[P164]
“You. Move.”

[P165]
I answered calmly.

[P166]
“Me. Don’t want to.”

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
